name: Schizophrenia
summary: Chronic psychotic disorder with positive symptoms (hallucinations, delusions, disorganization), negative symptoms, and cognitive impairment. Nearly all approved agents are dopamine D2 antagonists or partial agonists; xanomeline-trospium (2024) is the first muscarinic agent, and clozapine is the only drug labeled for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and reducing suicidal behavior.
plainSummary: Schizophrenia is a long-term brain illness that can cause hearing voices, false beliefs, and trouble thinking clearly. Many medicines, taken as pills, patches, or shots every few weeks to months, can control symptoms and prevent relapse.

approved.indication: Treatment of schizophrenia (adults and adolescents 13 years and older).

population.ages: Adults and pediatric patients 13 years and older

dosing.start: Adults 10–15 mg/day; adolescents 2 mg/day
dosing.notes: Known CYP2D6 poor metabolizers: half the usual dose. Halve dose with strong CYP2D6 or CYP3A4 inhibitors; double with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Opipza oral film dissolves on the tongue.

Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults (antidepressant class warning)
